Subject: Reserved commit discussion — sizing attachment + timing

Samir —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Per our demo, HydraEdge's production peaks (batch + interactive) look like they'll need roughly 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs sustained for 95th pct throughput, plus a staging buffer for retraining and TTS workloads. Attaching a quick sizing workbook so you can play with ramp scenarios (HydraEdge_Sizing.xlsx).

Questions from our side to prepare a tidy proposal:
- Do you expect a hard ship date requirement for the Dedicated pool (e.g., must be live by Jan 15)?
- Is a single-region (us-west) deployment acceptable for the initial phase?
- Any regulatory requirements that would prevent a standard Dedicated contract?

I'll sketch three reserved-commit options (12/24/36) with corresponding buydown discounts and ramp windows once you confirm the start flexibility.

Thanks,

Cc: Maya Patel <maya@hydraedge.ai>, procurement@hydraedge.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit discussion — sizing attachment + timing

Michael —

Thanks for the workbook. We ran a couple of scenarios: the team wants to avoid any hard penalty if our internal migration hits delays (supply chain / infra readiness). We can commit to a 24-month term in principle, but need a 60–90 day soft start window where billing only begins once we flip to live traffic. In that soft-start window we'd still like guaranteed access to a staging buffer (at reduced billable rate) to run pre-prod tests.

Confirming: single-region is OK for now, target commercial go-live window is Feb–Mar 2027.

Can you include a breakdown showing: committed GPU-hours per month, the effective per-GPU-hour price at each commit level, and an example credit if the start slips by >30 days?

—Samir
Samir Rao
Head of Platform | HydraEdge
samir@hydraedge.ai

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@hydraedge.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit discussion — sizing attachment + timing

Samir —

Appreciate the clarity. Below is an initial commercial structure we can formalize into a proposal:

Summary (pro forma):
- Option A (12-mo): 8 GPU-equivalents guaranteed; baseline rate $45/GPU-hour; no buydown credit after start; minimal staging buffer 1 GPU included.
- Option B (24-mo): 8 GPU-equivalents guaranteed; baseline rate $40/GPU-hour; 12% buydown applied if they commit to the full 24 mo and adhere to a ramp schedule (see ramp bullets).
- Option C (36-mo): 8 GPU-equivalents guaranteed; baseline rate $37/GPU-hour; 18% buydown on committed baseline.

Ramp & start guidance (recommended):
- Soft start window: up to 60 days from contract execution where billing only begins on full traffic cutover, but we provide a staging buffer at 50% bill rate for up to 2 GPUs (to validate).
- Ramp schedule (for buydown eligibility): month 1 = 25% baseline, month 2 = 50%, month 3 = 75%, month 4 = 100% of committed baseline. If ramp falls behind more than one full month vs schedule, buydown resets to a reduced tier (we can detail T&Cs).
- Start-credit: if production-start misses the agreed live-by date by >30 days and Redwood is unable to provide capacity due to provisioning delays, we offer a prorated credit equal to 25% of billed baseline for the delayed month.

SLA / throughput guarantees:
- Target p95 latency SLO for interactive traffic: 250ms (single-region).
- Throughput guarantee: defined as sustained token throughput per GPU; we'll include the calibrated profile in the formal proposal.

Attachments: I attached a committed-terms PDF with price tiers (RG-commit-options-v2.pdf) and will mirror the ramp schedule in the MSA.

If this maps to HydraEdge's priorities, I can convert to a draft with explicit numbers (monthly GPU-hour commitments) and send to procurement for redlines.

Best,
Michael

Attachment: RG-commit-options-v2.pdf (proposal stub)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@hydraedge.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit discussion — sizing attachment + timing

Samir —

Two quick internal clarifications from our side:
1) For a 24-month commit we can extend the soft start to 90 days (instead of 60) provided HydraEdge signs off on the ramp milestones and accepts a small staging premium for months in the soft window (we typically price that at 50% of baseline for staging GPUs).
2) On the credit: we'd prefer to commit to a service credit schedule in the MSA (0.5 days SLA credit per calendar day of missed guaranteed capacity beyond 30 days) rather than a flat prorated refund — that keeps the remedy tied to uptime. We can work examples into the contract redline.

If HydraEdge needs added protection we can also propose a small refundable start deposit that gets applied to the first invoice or returned if start slips >120 days.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Dedicated Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Samir Rao <samir@hydraedge.ai>

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit discussion — sizing attachment + timing

Thanks Michael / Lauren —

24 months is our preferred term. A few asks from procurement before we proceed to signature:
- Can you show the exact monthly GPU-hour commitment and the net effective $/GPU-hour after the 12% buydown (example calculation for our 8-unit baseline)?
- We want the soft-start billing trigger to be "production cutover" rather than a fixed calendar date.
- If Redwood requires a refundable deposit, cap it at 10% of the first three months' committed spend.
- For the staging buffer, we propose Redwood guarantee access (best-effort, within region) to up to 2 GPUs during the soft-start window at 25% of baseline (HydraEdge will pay for them if used).

If you can send a slightly updated proposal showing those line items we can route to legal and procurement for sign-off.

—Samir

Attachment: procurement-reqs.pdf (they attached a short procurement checklist)
